newsitem.title: USA: Abercrombie & Fitch soars after IPO.
newsitem.headline: Abercrombie & Fitch soars after IPO.

text.p: The stock of Abercrombie & Fitch Co. shot up almost 45 percent on Thursday as the casual wear retailer made its debut on the New York Stock Exchange.

Trading in Abercrombie & Fitch, renowned for its rugged, outdoor wear since 1892, opened at $22 a share, up $6 from its offering price of $16 and rose as high as $23.25 as investors made it the second most heavily traded issue on the NYSE. In late trading the stock was up $7 at $23.

Analysts had said investors would be attracted by Abercrombie's casual wear brand and its consistent earnings growth, which have made it one of the jewels in the Limited Inc.'s $7.9 billion retailing empire.
"This is hot, hot, hot," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket newsletter, said of the initial public offering.

Abercrombie, which outfitted the safaris of Teddy Roosevelt, Ernest Hemingway and the expeditions of Admiral Byrd to the North and South Poles, has been repositioning itself since 1992 to appeal to a more youthful, fashion-conscious audience.
The Reynoldsville, Ohio-based company reported 1995 sales of $235.7 million, up 42 percent from 1994 sales of $165.5 million.

The Limited bought Abercrombie & Fitch from Oshman's Sporting Goods Inc. in 1988. In recent years, Abercrombie has outperformed most of the Limited's other units, including Limited Express and Limited Too. Even after the IPO, Limited will still hold about 95 percent of Abercrombie's voting power.
